children: in a report on Wednesday that the gap between home sellers and buyers widened to its highest level since 2013.
There were an estimated 62.6% more home sellers than buyers in the U.S. housing market in September, according to the report.
September marks the fourth record-breaking month in a row.
The gap widened because buyers pulled back, while sellers kept showing up. There were an estimated 928,892 homebuyers in the market, the lowest level in records since 2013.
The number is down 2.4% from a month earlier, the fifth straight monthly decline.
Meanwhile, there were an estimated 1,510,784 sellers, the most since March 2020 and up 1.2% month over month.
Huge seller surpluses are seen in Miami, Nashville, TN, and a handful of Texas metros. On the other hand, Sun Belt tops the extreme buyer's market.

"This is a buyer's market born out of caution, not strength," said Asad Khan, a senior economist at Redfin. "Buyers have tremendous negotiating power in most of the country because so many other would-be buyers have been priced out of the market, or scared off by economic uncertainty."
